newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria letter bomb aimed at minister's relative.
newsitem.headline: Austria letter bomb aimed at minister's relative.

text.p: A letter bomb which exploded in Vienna on Monday was addressed to the step-mother of Interior Minister Caspar Einem, the Interior Ministry said.
A woman -- not Einem's step-mother -- called police after she received the suspicious package. The device exploded after bomb disposal experts took the package away at around 6 p.m. (1700 GMT).
Einem's step-mother, Lotte Ingrisch, used to write librettos for Einem's father, composer Gottfried von Einem, who died in July, aged 78.
It was still unclear how the device ended up in the home of the so-far unidentified woman in the working class district of Favoriten in the east of Vienna.

No group has yet claimed responsibility for sending the device, but the so-called Bajuwarian Liberation Army (BLA) has said it sent more than a score of letter bombs over the past three years, injuring 12 people, mostly foreigners or figures linked to immigration or refugee issues.
"This is the beginning of the sixth series of letter bombs," Robert Sturm, the chief of the Interior Ministry bomb investigation unit, told Austrian television.
